indexing.note: fixed bands (W. Va. Code 11-21-4i); 2026 rates lower (11-21-4j)

not_modelled.what: Retirement of a federal law enforcement officer or fireman is not taxed (line 30). A projection does not know this service, so the pension gets only the 2,000 of line 33.

Retirement from a West Virginia state or local police, deputy sheriffs' or firemen's system is not taxed (line 31). A projection does not know this service, so the pension gets only the 2,000 of line 33.
PBGC Modification (line 45): the benefit lost when a defined benefit plan terminated and its guarantor pays less is subtracted. A projection does not hold the benefit the plan would have paid.
Line 47 for a person under 65 certified as permanently and totally disabled: the same 8,000 as the senior deduction. A projection does not know disability.
Surviving spouse deduction (line 48): a one-time subtraction of up to 8,000, shared with line 47, the year after the death of a spouse who was 65 or disabled.
One additional 2,000 exemption for a surviving spouse for the two years after the year of death.
500 on line 6 when zero exemptions are claimed. Applies to a filer another person claims as a dependent, not to the households a projection holds.
Low-Income Earned Income Exclusion (line 5): the smaller of federal AGI, earned income or 10,000 (5,000 married filing separately), only with federal AGI at or under that maximum.
Family Tax Credit: a percentage of the tax by family size and Modified Federal AGI, 100% up to 21,150 for a couple and 15,650 for one person, and none over 23,850 and 18,350. A low-income credit.
Interest or dividends on U.S. obligations, and West Virginia bonds subject to federal tax, are subtracted (line 29). A projection cannot tell them from other interest.
Active duty military pay of a called-up Guard or Reserve member (line 36) and in the year of separation (line 37). A projection does not know these wages.

approximations.what: Line 47 takes that person's lines 29 through 34 off the 8,000, so together they come to the higher of the two. The format cannot say that: cap_reduced_by takes off benefits received, and line 34 is only the taxable benefits at 65% or 100%. So the Social Security subtraction and the age 65 deduction share a best_of_group, each person's larger one counting, with the 8,000 reduced by military retirement. That is exact for Social Security and military retirement. Line 33 stays outside the group because a person under 65 keeps it alongside Social Security, and a whole public pension can't be taken off the 8,000 when only 2,000 of it is on line 33.
approximations.size: Only for a person 65 or older with a line 33 pension whose Social Security and military lines add to under 8,000: the deduction is too large by up to the line 33 amount. At most 2,000 x 4.82% = 96 a year for each person. None once those lines reach 8,000.

approximations.what: The 2025 rule is held in later years. The Tax Division page says the share above the AGI limit becomes 100% in tax year 2026. Scheduled changes are a pending feature (tax-reference-data issue #2).
approximations.size: Only above the AGI limit. Single, AGI 80,000, taxable benefits 30,000: 19,500 is subtracted here and 30,000 from 2026, so 10,500 x 4.82% = 506 too much tax a year.

approximations.what: A pension from a West Virginia police, deputy sheriffs' or firemen's system, or a federal law enforcement or fire pension, is treated as a line 33 pension (not_modelled entries).
approximations.size: Nearly the whole pension's tax. A 40,000 pension: 38,000 stays taxed, up to 1,832 a year at 4.82%. For a person 65 or older the 8,000 deduction taken here offsets up to 386 of that.

approximations.what: Line 33 is applied to every public_pension. The booklet names only the West Virginia Teachers' and Public Employees' systems and Federal Retirement.
approximations.size: At most 2,000 x 4.82% = 96 a year for each person with another West Virginia public pension.

approximations.what: Line 47 column (c) leaves out income on lines 35 to 46, such as railroad retirement. The projection offsets the person's own income without that test.
approximations.size: Only for a person 65 or older with under 8,000 of other income who also has such income. At most 386 a year.

approximations.what: Interest on U.S. obligations is taxed (the projection cannot tell it from other interest).
All municipal bond interest is treated as from other states (added and taxed); West Virginia's own bonds are not added.

Tax below 100,000 of taxable income is figured on the exact income, where the booklet uses a Tax Table row's midpoint rounded to the whole dollar. Other tax is also rounded to the whole dollar in the booklet.
approximations.size: About 2 dollars at most: rows are up to 100 wide.

approximations.what: The Family Tax Credit is not applied (not_modelled entry).
approximations.size: Only under 23,850 of Modified Federal AGI for a couple or 18,350 for one person, where the tax is small. A couple under 65 at 21,150 with no subtractions shows 434 of tax and owes none.

approximations.what: The disability deduction, the surviving spouse deduction and exemption, and the Low-Income Earned Income Exclusion are not applied (not_modelled entries).
approximations.size: 8,000 x 4.82% = 386 for a year of the disability or surviving spouse deduction; 2,000 x 4.82% = 96 for a year of the exemption; the exclusion is under 482.
